Interesting! Actually I think the `Clone()` wasn't required either way, it also seems to work fine with the original `Environment(tools=["default"])`.

The issue in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/101715/files#r1920844908 was due to `mingw` not being properly set as custom tool when just doing `scons p=windows` on Linux, because our logic for that was incomplete. Why it worked before our PRs though, I'm not sure.

> The issue in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/101715/files#r1920844908 was due to `mingw` not being properly set as custom tool when just doing `scons p=windows` on Linux, because our logic for that was incomplete. Why it worked before our PRs though, I'm not sure.

Actually I think the reason it failed in #101715 is because of the removal of `default` here:
```
custom_tools = []
if env["platform"] == "android":
    custom_tools += ["clang", "clang++", "as", "ar", "link"]
elif env["platform"] == "web":
    custom_tools += ["cc", "c++", "ar", "link", "textfile", "zip"]
elif env["platform"] == "windows" and methods.get_cmdline_bool("use_mingw", False):
    custom_tools += ["mingw"]
for tool in custom_tools:
    env.Tool(tool)
```
Since the last `elif` didn't match `scons p=windows` on Linux (no explicit `use_mingw`), and it no longer fell back to `default`, that caused the error.

So I'm still unsure whether it's a good idea to do `tools=[]` and then register some custom tools, or `tools=["default"]` to have sane defaults and then add custom tools in specific cases (like we currently do in `master`).
